To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) cochlear implant users with open-set speech perception demonstrated larger dynamic ranges than those without open-set speech perception, 2) the dynamic range of cochlear implant users was related to the size of their evoked potential responses recorded from the cochlear nucleus and auditory cortex, and 3) cochlear implant recipients who had open-set speech perception showed a change in the size (amplitude) of the dynamic range when stimulus rate was changed.

1) cochlear implant subjects with open-set speech recognition have larger and more robust evoked potentials recorded at multiple levels of the auditory system, and 2) the inability to follow the changes in the temporal structure of the electrical stimulation is associated with poor speech recognition performance

the neurophysiologic measures (EABR Wave V amplitude, EABR Wave V latency, EAMLR Na-Pa amplitude, EAMLR Pa-Na latency, EAMMR Na-Na latency, ELAR N1-P2 latency) and behavioral measures (dynamic range, speech recognition) were statistically different between subjects who could and could not perform open-set speech recognition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
relating neurophysiologic measures with behavioral performance of cochlear implant users.
the relationship between the neural response of cochlear implant subjects at the level of the auditory nerve and the auditory brainstem.
relating neurophysiologic measures to the behavioral performance of cochlear implant patients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
speech perception performance in cochlear implant recipients is associated with the ability to follow temporal characteristics of the electrical stimulation.
speech perception performance in adult cochlear implant recipients is correlated with the presence of evoked potential responses at the cortical level of the auditory system.
cochlear implant recipients who demonstrate good speech perception have 1) a well-formed EABR, 2) a well-formed and larger amplitude EAMLR, and 3) a well-formed ELAR.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

cochlear implant recipients with open-set speech perception demonstrate a larger dynamic range, more robust electrophysiologic response amplitudes, and a greater ability to follow temporal variations in the stimulus.
the ability to perceive speech with a cochlear implant is related to a subject's neural encoding of electrical stimulation and to the neural synchrony required for the perception of speech.

the best performers had 1) larger dynamic ranges with larger changes in the dynamic range with stimulus rate, 2) larger EAMLR responses, 3) lower evoked threshold levels for the Na-P2 complex, 4) larger ELAR responses, 5) longer periods of stimulation, 6) better speech perception, and 7) shorter periods of deafness.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the neural encoding of the cochlear implant should provide sufficient physiologial responses of the central auditory system to perceive speech.
the neural responses to electrical stimulation are related to speech perception, but the exact relationship is complex.
the neural synchrony of the central auditory nervous system must be intact to perceive speech through electrical stimulation.
